properties.decision:
A property whose value is an id is NOT automatically a node reference. Four kinds exist in this design, measured 2026-08-29 across every `*_id` property with no minimum-instance floor, and only the first takes `node_ref: true`:

① **NODE REFERENCE** — names a node that must exist for the record to mean anything. Dangling is a real defect. `TemporalFact.subject_id` (334 values, 334 resolve). DECLARED.

② **HISTORICAL ANCHOR** — resolves when written, and is EXPECTED to stop resolving. The record exists to survive its target. `Snapshot.target_id` (196 values, 192 resolve; all 4 dangles correct). NOT DECLARED.

③ **COMPUTED-FINDING REFERENCE** — names something calculated and never stored as a node, so it resolves to nothing by construction. `Question.gap_id` (57 values, 0 resolve — the correct reading, not rot). NOT DECLARED.

④ **CROSS-DESIGN REFERENCE** — names a GRAPH rather than a node. `Resource.dependency_graph_id` (1 value, `dynograph-foundation`). NOT DECLARED, and not a declared property at all.

THE RULE THAT FOLLOWS: `node_ref` is applied only to ① — and where it is withheld, THE DECLARATION ITSELF SAYS WHY, in the schema description, because that is the text a reader meets. Done for `Snapshot.target_id` and `Question.gap_id`.

⚠️ THREE ARE DECLARED AND HAVE NEVER BEEN WRITTEN, so they are recorded as UNDECIDED rather than assigned: `ReadinessAssessment.target_id`, `DimensionAssessment.target_id`, `DimensionObservation.target_id`, all at zero instances. Whether a scored node's later deletion makes the assessment wrong (①) or leaves it as the surviving record of what was scored (②) is the same question, and there is no evidence to settle it. Decide when the first one is written.
properties.name: An id-valued property is one of four kinds, and only one of them is a node reference
properties.rationale:
Recorded on Anthony's word 2026-08-29 — "record the judgement for target_id and gap_id" — after `fact:which-properties-are-node-references-is-a-judgement-made-once-and-never-recorded-for-the-others` found the judgement had been made exactly once, for one property, and never written down for any other.

THREE NEAR-MATCHES WERE OFFERED AND ALL THREE READ IN FULL; THIS IS A DIFFERENT KIND OF RECORD. The two facts are MEASUREMENTS — one of the detection hole, one of the cause — and they keep their own numbers and caveats. `dec:a-restore-reports-an-unresolvable-reference-rather-than-refusing-it` is a decision about what an IMPORT does when it meets an unresolvable value. This is the standing rule about which properties are references AT ALL, which is upstream of both: it decides what the guard and the detector are even looking at.

THE DEFECT WAS THE SILENCE, NOT A MISSING FLAG. `subject_id` and `target_id` are declared identically — `type: string, required: true, indexed: true` — and differ only in `node_ref`. Nothing said why, so the next reader had two moves and both were bad: declare it, and a detector starts firing on correct history; leave it, and never learn the omission was deliberate. An unrecorded judgement is indistinguishable from an oversight, and this design has now spent three sessions rediscovering the same class because of it.

⭐ THE FOURTH KIND WAS FOUND BY DROPPING A THRESHOLD, WHICH IS WORTH KEEPING AS METHOD. The root-cause pass swept only the three properties `heal.rs` names, with a three-instance floor to filter noise. Re-run with no floor, `Resource.dependency_graph_id` appeared — one value, naming a graph rather than a node, undeclared in the schema entirely. A filter set to suppress noise had been suppressing a whole category, which is the same shape as the defect that started this thread: an instrument that looks complete because the cases it misses are the ones it cannot see.

WHY NOT SIMPLY DECLARE EVERYTHING THAT LOOKS LIKE A POINTER, which is the tempting simplification: it would refuse every Question this design has ever written (kind ③ resolves to nothing by construction) and make `dangling_reference` report four correct historical records as defects (kind ②). A rule that fires on correct work is worse than no rule — the standing judgement behind `supporting is not conflict` and behind the `required`-designation skip in `unprovided_interface`.

THE THREE UNDECIDED ONES ARE LEFT UNDECIDED ON PURPOSE. Guessing a `node_ref` for a type with zero instances would assert a rule nobody could have tested, at exactly the moment there is no evidence — and a wrong guess would be discovered by the first person to write one, as a refusal they cannot act on.
